items.title: Earl King Interview, 1980-04-10
items.q: Allen's just something? Yeah, with everything, man, because he was somewhat like Ray Charles.

ctx.x: Can you say something in general about the use of the guitar in the Wallace music? Outside of the solo instrument? How was the guitar was used in the Wallace music?

Well, predominantly, if you had listened at some of the older records, especially the ones during the 60s, and you hear the records that were produced around here, you would hear rhythm support, nothing but stuff like, you said, what the government... You know, what the double is going on there? But that was that little light blood right in there. Those jinx with the things that they were using right in the things in there. And the other one was... As a matter of fact, Allen used that predominant everything.…

Yeah. A lot of times, a lot of times, the bass was lost in a lot of recordings. Yeah. The fidelity of the mixing. So, uh, so we could say, maybe people look at all the instruments. We said the guitar was basically a rhythm instrument in New Orleans music. The bass and the drums, uh, carry the rhythm. And, uh, the horns, it seems the horns and the piano were basically the solo instruments. Yeah. And, uh, did, took care of most of the solos. Yeah. Um. Whereas in, in other parts of the country, Chicago, the guitar…
